purpose: Assesses whether the organization can limit or recover from an adversary's attempts to manipulate, interrupt, or destroy systems and data.
summary: Impact consists of techniques adversaries use to disrupt availability or compromise integrity, such as data destruction, ransomware encryption, denial of service, or manipulating business or operational processes to achieve a disruptive or destructive goal.
expectedStatementElements: How the organization backs up critical data and systems, and how those backups are protected from being encrypted or destroyed alongside production data
What resilience or failover capabilities limit the impact of a denial-of-service or destructive attack on availability
How the organization detects and responds to signs of ransomware or mass encryption/deletion activity in progress
How business and operational process integrity is verified so subtle manipulation (rather than outright destruction) would be caught
evidenceExamples: Backup architecture documentation showing offline/immutable backups isolated from production credentials
Business continuity/disaster recovery plan and recent test results
Ransomware/mass-encryption detection configuration and response playbook
Process integrity verification or reconciliation controls for critical business processes
commonGaps: Backups are reachable using the same credentials as production, so they could be encrypted or deleted in the same attack
No tested failover or resilience plan exists for a destructive or denial-of-service event
Mass encryption or deletion activity isn't detected until the impact is already widespread
Business process integrity isn't independently verified, so subtle manipulation could go unnoticed for a long time
interviewQuestions: Could the same attacker who compromised production also reach and destroy your backups?
Has your disaster recovery or failover plan actually been tested, not just documented?
Would mass encryption or deletion get caught early, or only after the damage is already done?
How would you catch someone quietly manipulating a business process rather than destroying something outright?
